note: Reflex policy pack: eks (Kubernetes on EKS). Copy it with `reflex policy init --pack eks`, then commit .reflex/policy.json. It only adds checks. deny rules block in every mode; ask rules go to a human, and in the autonomous profile never to System 2. Patterns are case-insensitive and read the command plus its context (kube_context=, aws_profile=, cwd=). The prod markers treat a kube context or AWS profile whose name contains prod as production, so a command there that is not read-only asks; EKS contexts are often ARNs such as arn:aws:eks:eu-west-1:123456789012:cluster/prod-eu, which match too. Rename them to match your clusters. For a server-side dry run before deletes, also set "infra": {"kubectl_diff": true} in your own config.json.

rules.rule: deletes an EKS cluster or node group
rules.note: deny: a cluster delete takes every workload on it. Do it by hand, through your IaC.

rules.rule: deletes every resource of a kind in a namespace or across the cluster
rules.note: deny: kubectl delete --all or -A removes more than anyone reviews. Name the resources.

rules.rule: deletes a namespace, volume, stateful set or CRD
rules.note: ask: these hold data, and a CRD delete removes every custom resource of that type.
ask: evicts or stops scheduling pods on the node.

rules.rule: scales a workload to zero replicas
rules.note: ask: scaling to zero is an outage for that workload.

rules.rule: changes cluster RBAC or the aws-auth config map
rules.note: ask: RBAC and aws-auth decide who can do anything in the cluster.

rules.rule: uninstalls or rolls back a Helm release
rules.note: ask: uninstall removes the release's resources, rollback redeploys an older one.

always_human.rule: a cluster RBAC or aws-auth change
always_human.note: never approved by System 2 in the autonomous profile, always a human
